methods.label: Read the fractional part and disk
methods.explanation:
The definition of the greatest integer gives
\[
[t]\le t<[t]+1,
\]
so \(T=t-[t]\) satisfies \(0\le T<1\). The inequality \((x-T)^2+y^2\le T^2\) describes the closed disk with center \((T,0)\) and radius \(T\). If \(T=0\), it consists only of the origin and has area zero. Otherwise, its area is \(\pi T^2\). Therefore, in all cases,
\[
0\le \operatorname{Area}(S)=\pi T^2<\pi.
\]
This proves statement B, whose upper bound allows equality even though equality is never attained.

The origin satisfies the defining inequality for every \(t\), so A is false. For \(t=11/2\), the center is \((1/2,0)\), which is not on \(y=x\), and the disk contains \((1/2,-1/2)\), which is outside the first quadrant. Thus C and D are also false. The answer is \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
